raw_affiliation_strings: Reader in Archaeology at the University of Reading (Whiteknights, P.O. Box 218, Reading RG6 6AA, U.K. [M.A. [email protected]]). Born in 1949, he was educated at the University of Göttingen (M.A., 1975; Ph.D., 1988) and the University of Oxford (Dip. Archaeol., 1977; M. Litt., 1979). He has been a lecturer in archaeology at Queen's University of Belfast and a visiting lecturer at the University of Kiel. His research interests include early medieval burial rites, migrations and ethnogenesis, the history of archaeological thought in Germany, and a current fieldwork project in the North Caucasus. Among his publications are Settlement Types and Settlement Patterns in the West Hallstatt Province (British Archaeological Reports International Series S57), Angelsächsische Waffengräber des 5. bis 7. Jahrhunderts (Zeitschrift für Archäologie des Mittelalters Beiheft 6, 1992), “All Quiet on the Western Front? Paradigms, Methods, and Approaches in West German Archaeology,” in Archaeological Theory in Europe: The Last Three Decades, edited by I. Hodder (London and New York: Routledge, 1991), and Archaeology, Ideology, and Society: The German Experience (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, forthcoming). The present paper was submitted 8 XI 96 and accepted 15 II 97
